lina (Docs): opened a PR to consolidate 429/timeout troubleshooting + a short migration note for the context-trim SDK helpers. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4902

mike (SRE): thanks. does the repro target hosted only or dedicated too? we see different Retry-After shapes on Dedicated.

lina (Docs): good point1: PR includes test steps for hosted and a dedicated-run checklist (note about capacity-based 429s). TL;DR: run the rps-fanout script against the small model, wait for the first 429s, capture Retry-After and X-RateLimit-* headers.

chris (SDK): can we include a tiny helper that shows trimming oldest messages vs summarizing history? customers keep asking which to prefer.

lina (Docs): added two short examples. JS snippet shows dropping oldest tokens, Python shows a naive summarizer that calls a compacting endpoint.

chris (SDK): small tweak to the JS stream example: show how to compute token count with our tokenizer helper and then slice messages accordingly. I'll push a one-line change.

lina (Docs): pasted the JS trimming example in the PR body for visibility: 
```js
// trim-oldest.js (snippet)
const {tokenize} = require('@redwood/tokenizer')
function trimHistory(messages, maxTokens) {
  let count = messages.reduce((s,m) => s + tokenize(m.text).length, 0)
  while (count > maxTokens) {
    const removed = messages.shift() // drop oldest message
    count -= tokenize(removed.text).length
  }
  return messages
}
```

pat (Eng): one operational caveat: when trimming for streaming retries, include the active partial buffer in your token count so you don't accidentally resend overlapping tokens. add a note.

mike (SRE): linking to runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/rl-429#capacity-vs-burst please make sure anchor exists. also add example curl for header capture: 
```bash
for i in {1..500}; do curl -i -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate; sleep 0.02; done
```

lina (Docs): added the curl example and fixed the runbook anchor link. also added a small table in docs recommending fallback routing policies: fallback to small-model with rate-based throttle, or queue with token-based admission.

chris (SDK): I've pushed the token-count line and a comment about preferring summarization when semantic fidelity is critical. also noted that Retry-After header should be respected before exponential backoff.

docs-lint-bot: lina updated files: docs/troubleshooting/429-and-timeouts.md, snippets/trim-oldest.js, snippets/compact_summarize_py.py
